entities.summary: William Worcester was an English antiquary, author, and historian known for his detailed writings on medieval England. Born into a family of modest means, Worcester served as the secretary to Sir John Fastolf, a prominent military commander during the Hundred Years' War, and later compiled extensive notes on English history, geography, and heraldry. Worcester's extensive collection of manuscripts, including his own translations and commentaries, were widely studied and admired during his lifetime. His work had a lasting impact on the development of English historiography, influencing prominent scholars such as Sir Thomas Malory. Worcester's legacy can still be seen in the many institutions and organizations he helped establish, including the Royal Historical Society and the English Antiquarian Society. As a testament to his enduring influence, Worcester's manuscripts continue to be studied by scholars and researchers today.
